key_insight: Dirac-3S natively handles higher-order optimization, avoiding quadratization and gate compilation, but demonstrates a mapping-cost advantage rather than superior solution quality.
engineering_relevance: Native polynomial support could simplify encoding dense industrial objectives that incur prohibitive qubit or gate overhead on conventional quantum hardware.
method: Encode four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic optimization instances.
Run each instance natively on the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system with 30 samples.
Compare solutions with certified optima or classical best-known values and estimate conventional quantum mapping costs.
evidence_signal: Across 180 samples, all solutions were feasible; the best portfolio result was within 0.32% of its reference and the best budget result was 15% above its reference, with no sample reaching its reference.
watch_item: Classical solvers reached the references within minutes, and locally polished random starts were comparable or better; a time-to-solution advantage remains unproven.
paper_title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
